title: Add design-it-twice and spike craft to expertise planning.md
action: Two additive sections in .bee/expertise/planning.md, in its existing voice, with routing-table rows. (A) 'Design it twice' per CONTEXT.md D5, adapted from /home/thanhsmind/projects/AI/mattpocock-skill/skills/engineering/codebase-design/DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md (read it; rewrite for bee's swarm model, never copy): for a standard or high-risk shape whose interface is genuinely open, fan out 2-3 parallel read-only workers, each FORCED into a radically different design constraint (minimize the interface / optimize the common case / ports-and-adapters), each returning interface sketch + usage example + what it hides + tradeoffs; the orchestrator compares by depth, locality, and seam placement and recommends ONE with a stated reason — an opinionated read, not a menu; skip the move entirely when the shape's interface is already dictated by locked decisions or existing patterns. (B) 'Spike craft' per D7, adapted from prototype/SKILL.md, LOGIC.md, UI.md (read all three): a spike answers exactly ONE named question, written down before building; a logic/state question gets a minimal pure module plus the thinnest runnable shell; a UI/shape question gets 2-3 STRUCTURALLY different variants (visual tweaks of one structure answer nothing); no tests, no error handling beyond runnability, no abstractions — polish on throwaway code is waste; on completion the validated decision is captured (decision log / CONTEXT.md) and folds into real work, the spike itself never merges — it stays under .bee/spikes/ or a throwaway branch as a primary source to cite. Skip anything the file already states (check first — it already has walking-skeleton and smaller-path content nearby).
goal: Planning craft gains an interface-exploration move that fits the existing swarm model, and the spike lane gets its missing HOW.
verify: commands.test green (PATH cargo test --release); sections in file voice; no duplication of walking-skeleton material.
